scenes.title: Key ideas
items: Tight but realistic slippage (e.g. 0.1–0.5% for liquid majors, more only when you…
MEV-protected / private transaction routing (many wallets and aggregators offer this)
Don't broadcast huge swaps in illiquid pairs
scenes.vo: M.E.V. (maximal extractable value) is profit taken by whoever orders transactions in a block. Some is harmless (arbitrage realigning prices). The kind that hurts you: (pushing the price up), lets your trade execute at the worse price, then sells just after. Your slippage tolerance is its profit ceiling. Defences: First, Sandwich attack: a bot sees your pending swap, buys just before you. Next, Tight but realistic slippage (for example 0.1 to 0.5% for liquid majors, more only when you understand why). Then, M.E.V.-protected or private transaction routing (many wallets and aggregators offer this). Also, Split large trades. Avoid thin pools. And finally, Don't broadcast huge swaps in illiquid pairs.
scenes.cap: MEV (maximal extractable value) is profit taken by whoever orders transactions in a block. Some is harmless (arbitrage realigning prices). The kind that hurts you: (pushing the price up), lets your trade execute at the worse price, then sells just after. Your slippage tolerance is its profit ceiling. Defences: First, Sandwich attack: a bot sees your pending swap, buys just before you. Next, Tight but realistic slippage (e.g. 0.1–0.5% for liquid majors, more only when you understand why). Then, MEV-protected / private transaction routing (many wallets and aggregators offer this). Also, Split large trades. Avoid thin pools. And finally, Don't broadcast huge swaps in illiquid pairs.

scenes.title: Worked example
scenes.vo: Swapping $20,000: Too tight a tolerance (for example 0.05% on a volatile pair) just makes the transaction fail, and failed transactions still cost gas (Lesson 1.2). 3%: up to about $600. 0.5%: up to about $100. Private or protected route: Transaction isn't visible in the public mempool, so it can't be sandwiched from there.
scenes.cap: Swapping $20,000: Too tight a tolerance (e.g. 0.05% on a volatile pair) just makes the transaction fail, and failed transactions still cost gas (Lesson 1.2). 3%: up to ~$600. 0.5%: up to ~$100. Private / protected route: Transaction isn't visible in the public mempool, so it can't be sandwiched from there.

scenes.title: Checklist
items: Slippage set for this pair and size, never left at a high default
Protected routing on for larger swaps
Large orders split or routed through deep liquidity

scenes.q: What limits how much a sandwich bot can take?
scenes.a: Your slippage tolerance (and the pool's depth).

scenes.q: Why not set slippage near zero?
scenes.a: Normal price movement makes the transaction revert, and you still pay gas.
